# Contents {.unnumbered}

<!-- Generated by tools/make-contents.py from the book configuration
and chapter files on every build. Edit those, not this file. -->

Every part and chapter of the book on one page, in reading order, each
chapter with a one-line summary.

- [Copyright](copyright.qmd)
- [Preface](preface.qmd)
- [Conventions](conventions.qmd)
- [1 Introduction](00-intro.qmd)

## Part I. [Why and With Whom](part-1.qmd) {.unnumbered}

- [2 Why Reproducible Research](01-why.qmd)\
  Distinguishes methods, results, and inferential reproducibility, and
  names the check that makes each common failure loud.
- [3 Team Science for Biostatisticians](03-team-science.qmd)\
  Runs the intake conversation, places an engagement on the
  collaboration spectrum, and settles authorship.
- [4 De-identification and Data Ethics](02b-deidentification.qmd)\
  Sets out the HIPAA de-identification pathways, what each costs the
  analysis, and the obligations that survive de-identification.

## Part II. [Your Toolkit](part-2.qmd) {.unnumbered}

- [5 The Unix Shell](04b-shell.qmd)\
  Teaches the Unix shell: moving around the filesystem, inspecting a raw
  file before R reads it, and composing pipelines.
- [6 Setting Up Your Workstation](04-workstation.qmd)\
  Installs R, an IDE, Quarto, and Git, and verifies the machine with a
  checklist.
- [7 Git and GitHub for Solo Developers](05-git-solo.qmd)\
  Introduces Git and GitHub for a single analyst who wants a recoverable
  history.
- [8 Git for Teams](05b-git-teams.qmd)\
  Extends that history to a team: branches, pull requests, review, and
  conflicts.
- [9 AI-Assisted Coding](21-ai-coding.qmd)\
  Sets out how to prompt language models and coding agents, how to check
  what they produce, and what may be sent to them. It comes before the
  chapters in which you rely on them.

## Part III. [Data in Hand](part-3.qmd) {.unnumbered}

- [10 Getting Data In: Files](12b-acquisition.qmd)\
  Reads a clinical export with a full column specification and asserts
  against its usual pathologies.
- [11 APIs, Scraping, and Freezing What You Receive](12c-apis.qmd)\
  Queries web interfaces with `httr2` and freezes what was received.
- [12 Data Wrangling Essentials](13-wrangling.qmd)\
  Recodes per-site conventions and reports how many rows each step
  removes.
- [13 Factors, Strings, and Dates](14-types.qmd)\
  Handles factors, free-text strings, and dates.
- [14 Writing and Debugging Functions](14b-functions.qmd)\
  Turns a repeated cleaning step into a tested function, and shows how
  to find the cause when one misbehaves.
- [15 Joining and Reshaping](15-joins.qmd)\
  Predicts and checks the row count of every join.
- [16 Databases and SQL for Biostatisticians](15b-databases.qmd)\
  Queries a database with SQL and `dbplyr`.
- [17 Plotting with ggplot2 and purrr](16-graphics.qmd)\
  Builds figures with `ggplot2` and many figures at once with `purrr`.
- [18 Missing Data: Diagnosis, Imputation, Reporting](17-missing.qmd)\
  Diagnoses missing data, imputes it with `mice`, and runs a sensitivity
  analysis.
- [19 De-identification in Practice](02c-deident-practice.qmd)\
  Applies the rules of @sec-deident to a release, with assertions that
  fail if an identifier survives.

## Part IV. [Documents and Environments](part-4.qmd) {.unnumbered}

- [20 Reproducible Reports with Quarto](11-quarto.qmd)\
  Writes the analysis as a Quarto document whose numbers are computed
  rather than typed.
- [21 renv for Package Management](08-renv.qmd)\
  Records the package versions the analysis used in a lockfile and
  restores them elsewhere.
- [22 Docker for Reproducibility](09-docker.qmd)\
  Pins the R version, operating system, and system libraries in a
  container.
- [23 Assembling the Compendium](10-zzcollab.qmd)\
  Assembles the pieces into a research compendium and audits it against
  the Five Pillars.
- [24 Reproducible Pipelines with targets](10b-targets.qmd)\
  Turns the analysis into a pipeline that rebuilds only what an edit has
  invalidated.
- [25 Cloud Compute and Remote Servers](06-cloud.qmd)\
  Moves a job to a cluster or a cloud instance when a laptop is not
  enough.

## Part V. [Analysis Practice](part-5.qmd) {.unnumbered}

- [26 Statistical Analysis Plans](18-analysis-plan.qmd)\
  States the estimand, writes the statistical analysis plan and the data
  management and sharing plan, and uses a Git tag to show that the plan
  preceded the data.
- [27 Testing and Continuous Integration](20-testing.qmd)\
  Writes `tinytest` tests that assert values rather than shapes, and
  runs them on every push with GitHub Actions.

## Part VI. [Industry](part-6.qmd) {.unnumbered}

- [28 Clinical Data Standards: CDISC, SDTM, and ADaM](19-cdisc.qmd)\
  Traces a trial's data from the case report form through SDTM and ADaM
  to the tables of a clinical study report, and derives two ADaM
  datasets in R.
- [29 SAS for R Programmers](22-sas.qmd)\
  Teaches enough SAS to read a program and its log, write the R
  equivalent, and predict where the two fits of one model will disagree.

## Part VII. [Analysis to Audience](part-7.qmd) {.unnumbered}

- [30 Case Study: Palmer Penguins](23-penguins.qmd)\
  Works a complete analysis on the Palmer penguins data and maps each
  step to the chapter that taught it.
- [31 Case Study: ADNI MCI Prediction](24-adni.qmd)\
  Works a harder case, prediction of conversion from mild cognitive
  impairment, with data held under a data-use agreement.
- [32 Ethics Beyond Compliance](25d-ethics.qmd)\
  Argues that the reproducibility tools of this book cannot on their own
  keep an analysis from misleading its readers, and names the practices
  that can.
- [33 Communicating a Finished Analysis](25b-communicating.qmd)\
  Writes the answer-first memo and the response to reviewers.
- [34 Federal Requirements and Deposition](25c-federal.qmd)\
  Covers federal public-access requirements and the deposit of each
  artifact in a repository.

## Part VIII. [Capstone](part-8.qmd) {.unnumbered}

- [35 Capstone: HF-HOME from Export to Deposit](25-synthesis.qmd)\
  Takes the HF-HOME study from a multi-site case-report-form export to a
  deposited compendium with a tagged analysis plan, executed tests,
  continuous integration, a one-page memo, and a response to a reviewer.
  It is graded on the numbered habits of @sec-habits rather than on the
  estimate.
